signals.evidence: In Baram, community leaders expressed distrust in politicians and the army, stating they told unrealistic stories, promised a quiet and secure border but it did not happen in reality.
In Abdun/Maaleh Yosef, residents express that the army does not tell the truth.
In Liman/Matte Asher, sense of loss of trust in politicians and military personnel.
In Even Menahem/Maaleh Yosef, significant criticism toward the council; deep distrust in the authority.
In Baram, continuous stay in public shelters due to absence of individual safe rooms (ממ"דים); question raised whether shelters are suitable for continuous habitation.
In Goren/Maaleh Yosef, many people without individual safe rooms (ממ"דים); public shelters not in optimal condition; some residents have shelters far from their homes.
In Abdun/Maaleh Yosef, not all elderly have individual safe rooms (ממ"דים); public shelters are far away; no possibility to reach shelters in time.
In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, protection gaps exist; elderly lack protection.
In Even Menahem/Maaleh Yosef, serious problem with individual safe rooms (ממ"דים); public shelters in poor maintenance condition; no full operation of HFC system.
In Baram, shortage of appropriate public shelters (מקלטים) for operation, creating difficulty in running educational frameworks
In Psuta, 55% of homes lack protective fortification (מיגון); shortage of one public shelter that is unsuitable for use
In Kibbutz Eilon, low level of shelters: old systems, stuffy; no fortification in local clinic
In Yaara, public shelters serve prayer groups and informal frameworks but are too small to contain the activity, or defense policy does not permit (over 50 people)
In Baram, farmers reported limited number of protected field booths (מיגוניות) relative to the scope of agricultural land; request for regular supply of food products.
In Baram, lack of protected spaces for educational and social activities; no suitable public space available.
In Liman/Matte Asher, central distress regarding lack of children's activities; request for soldier-teacher support.
In Even Menahem/Maaleh Yosef, no spaces for social activities under protection; tourism not active; agriculture significantly affected.
In Kibbutz Eilon, need to restore medical/clinic response
In Baram, informal activity began today; HFC volunteer corps (צח"י) training and volunteer reinforcement requested.
In Abdun/Maaleh Yosef, HFC community coordinator recruiting volunteers; women's evening and activities for adults held.
In Even Menahem/Maaleh Yosef, community involvement and assistance when needed exists; limited number of volunteers.
In Baram, active Home Front Command (צח״י) volunteers present
In Psuta, volunteer network exists with many volunteers, though weak response and incomplete training
In Manot, Home Front Command (צח״י) and organizations bringing supplies and other services through WhatsApp
In Goren/Maaleh Yosef, young people fled; those aged 40+ remained.
In Yaara, those without a safe room (ממ"ד) self-evacuated; those with one shelter in place
In Goren/Maaleh Yosef, narrative of staying despite difficulties.
In Abdun/Maaleh Yosef, residents not leaving; community staying in place.
In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, most of the population returned to the settlement; young functioning population present; discourse of coping; community resilience with basic capacity.
In Matta/Maaleh Yosef, community cohesion significantly strengthened; overall sense of security.
In Psuta/Baram, there is resilience but political instability affecting it; people in emergency routine but more relaxed
In Manot/Maaleh Yosef, those interviewed were in elevated mood; less tension, less depressing to be there
In Goren/Maaleh Yosef, distress among elderly population; difficulty reaching safe rooms; some injured.

In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, elderly and those with special needs lack a single responsible entity; no entity holds a complete picture of elderly and disabled populations; welfare services not connected to this population; gap in mapping needs and difficulties; includes elderly residents, urban residents, families with special-needs children, and women whose families are mostly absent due to military service.

In Even Menahem/Maaleh Yosef, evidence of children struggling with difficulties; families without family support; no organized infrastructure for mapping needs and difficulties; urgent need for short-term resilience-building responses alongside long-term solutions.
In Psuta, clubs for elderly and special needs are closed and difficult to visit; they experience isolation and difficulty
In Horfish, frameworks not operating for elderly, women, and special populations; everything cancelled and only minimal activity via Zoom
In Yaara, requests to social services department for assistance to elderly
In Manot, elderly not visible; caring for each other within family framework
In Goren/Maaleh Yosef, increase in number of calls to emergency hotline 106.
In Psuta, welfare department finds it difficult to reach all residents for visits
In Goren/Maaleh Yosef, need for presence of soldier-teachers (מורות חיילות) for public information and guidance.
In Abdun/Maaleh Yosef, additional protected field booths (מיגוניות) provided.
In Abdun/Maaleh Yosef, informal activity taking place; children's activities expanded.
In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, community communication exists without evidence of toxic discourse; basic youth activity present; readiness unit exists.
In Horfish, private businesses opening and matters related to the council continuing, though with hardening of authority head's policy
In Liman/Matte Asher, HFC volunteer corps overall functioning well.
In Baram/Braam, community manager Angel Yitzhak, secretary Ilanit Kassos, and education coordinator Shir demonstrate strong leadership and cooperation among different role holders
In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, sense of fatigue and erosion from the ongoing situation; community resilience expressed as willingness to enable what is possible without distraction.
In Even Menahem/Maaleh Yosef, community under difficulties and deep erosion.
In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, good relationship with the council and Home Front Command.
In Horfish/Baram, authority broadcasts resilience and high control in the settlement; strong settlement with full emergency routine
In Netua, formal and informal leadership performing processes that build trust with the community

In Yaara, Home Front Command (צח״י) attempting population survey but only 5 out of over 250 families covered

In Even Menahem/Maaleh Yosef, sense of belonging alongside despair; painful to see families and children; significant disruption to daily routines.
In Matta/Maaleh Yosef, community members exited public shelter used as youth club and held rehearsals for a memorial evening for Mati Kaspi.
In Manot, apparently sent aid packages; their absence in current round is noticeable to residents met
In Matta/Maaleh Yosef, extensive protection in public space.
In Alqosh, approximately 70% of residents have a safe room (ממ"ד) in their private home; 10% have underground shelter in home; total of 8 public shelters in the settlement
In Baram, children and youth in homes use Zoom with limited success; workers not arriving; difficulty operating educational frameworks
In Yaara/Maaleh Yosef, silence in the street, almost no vehicles driving; no businesses open; those who remain are sheltering; people go out only if necessary
In Manot, no frameworks; desire for informal education or opening frameworks for kindergarten-elementary in settlement areas; not working except remotely
In Netua/Moshav, almost no movement of residents; residents in their homes; minimal movement of agricultural vehicles and almost no residents in the space
In Baram, complexities discovered regarding youth substance use and alcohol consumption
In Alqosh/Maaleh Yosef, residents are obedient regarding Home Front Command policy and directives
In Alqosh, 3 public shelters have problems requiring repair

In Horfish, isolation and difficulty reported among elderly, women, and special populations
In Kibbutz Eilon, sense of broken community cohesion following evacuation in Operation Iron Swords; residents more independent and less engaged in community activities
In Yaara, isolation and fatalistic attitude because there is no one to help them reach safe room when needed

In Kibbutz Eilon, many essential workers and feeling of uncertainty because there are no answers and no solutions for children of essential workers

In Manot, many mobilized to reserves; concerned and interested, communicating by phone
In Netua, residents do not want evacuation except parents with children where parents want it and children refuse; elderly want to stay home
In Netua, internal forces and Home Front Command (צח״י), community security officer, and readiness unit working in good communication

In Netua, alert warning affects people and they are near protected space; background noise of combat; feeling of pressure in homes; need to use shelter for sleep without risking going out at night without sufficient warning
In Baram, concern about business collapse (pizzeria mentioned).
In Baram, elderly population receiving community response.
